commons.description:
City flag of en:Long Beach, New York.
Image created by Gordon P. Hemsley on en:May 14, en:2005, based on a physical version of the flag.

Summary
The flag as described in the City of Long Beach Code of Ordinances, § 2-2:

Sec. 2-2. City flag described; use.


(a) The following design is hereby adopted as the design of the official flag of the city: A flag combining the colors of royal blue, white and gold, divided into two (2) diagonal segments of equal dimensions, one of royal blue and one of white, with the royal blue segment being over the white segment and nearest the flagstaff, together with the standard design of the seal of the city in gold upon a royal blue background, with white lettering, in the center of the flag, being equally in each segment; the whole being bound on all sides, except the side nearest the flagstaff, in gold fringe.


(b) The police department and the fire department are authorized to carry and display the official city flag at all their various functions, reviews, parades and receptions.


(Code 1957, §§ 2-104, 2-104.1)

commons.description:
The flag of Orestes, Indiana was created by Carolyn Shettle and was adopted by the Town Board in 1976. The rings represent continuity. One ring symbolizes the town's Delaware Indian heritage. One ring is for the gas boom that created the town, and one ring is for the more-than 300-year old Orestes oak tree. The rings are O’s, standing for Orestes. The flame represents the discovery of gas, and it also suggests the torch of liberty. The colors are red, white, and blue for freedom, and the blue is made brighter to also represent independence. Unintentionally, but clearly visible in blue, outlined by the flame, is a descending dove which symbolizes peace and Christianity.



Digital file made entirely by me.

commons.description:
Bandera del municipio de Saladoblanco (Huila).
La bandera está conformada por los colores blanco y verde. Que significan:

  Verde:del mismo tono que el de la bandera del Huila, expresa la fertilidad de los campos y la esperanza en el futuro, y está formada por triángulos equiláteros que se ubican en los extremo.
  Blanco:complementando el rectángulo, dos isósceles de este color que significan la paz, la fidelidad y honradez; que caracteriza a la etnia saladeña.
La Bandera es de las mismas proporciones del pabellón nacional (2:3)

Referencias: [1][2]
